summary: RETEST after CSP meta tag removal from inscricao.html and index.html. ALL 3 features PASS. Feature 1 (CEP autofill for 01310100): endereco='Avenida Paulista', bairro='Bela Vista', complemento='de 612 a 1510 - lado par', estado='São Paulo' -- all filled correctly via /api/cep proxy. Feature 2 (CEP 99999999 fallback): 404 handled gracefully, endereco/bairro/complemento remain editable (user can type manually), no UI freeze. Feature 3 (regression): / returns 200 and shows concurso content; /farpapainel/ returns 200. Browser console shows ZERO CSP errors ('violates the following Content Security Policy directive' completely gone). Only console warning is a benign 404 for /api/cep/99999999 which is expected.
critical_code_review_comments: Minor note: on invalid CEP (404), the code does not clear the previously autofilled endereco/bairro/complemento values -- they retain the last successful CEP's data. Fields ARE editable so the user can overwrite, which satisfies the fallback requirement. If desired, main agent could optionally clear these fields on 404 for a cleaner UX, but it is NOT a bug per the spec.
inscricao.html is still ~4MB due to base64-embedded SingleFile assets (Jivosite widget, fonts, images). Consider a future cleanup pass to strip unused inline assets.
context_for_next_testing_agent: CSP fix is fully verified working. inscricao.html has no more <meta http-equiv=content-security-policy> tags (grep -c returned 0 in both inscricao.html and index.html). /api/cep proxy call from browser now succeeds. Test values used: CEP 01310100 (valid, returns Av Paulista SP), CEP 99999999 (invalid, returns 404). Both handled correctly by frontend JS.

rca of the issue.bug: N/A - previous bug (CSP blocking /api/cep fetch) is fully resolved
rca of the issue.verification: 1) grep -c 'content-security-policy' in inscricao.html and index.html = 0 (zero occurrences). 2) Browser test: no CSP violation errors in console. 3) fetch('/api/cep/01310100') now succeeds and populates fields with correct ViaCEP data. 4) fetch('/api/cep/99999999') returns 404 handled gracefully, fields remain editable for manual entry.
